chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'Indeed, the day of Wednesday is fasted because no past community was punished except on the day of Wednesday, the middle of the month. Therefore, it is recommended to fast that day.'
ai.seo_question: Why is Wednesday recommended for fasting in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) establishes the recommendation (istikhāb) of fasting on Wednesday by linking it to the historical precedent of divine punishment befalling previous nations on this day, specifically noting its occurrence in the middle of the month. This tradition, found in al-Kāfī, underscores the concept of 'days of calamity' in Shia piety, where fasting serves as a means of expiation and spiritual protection against similar afflictions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘But rather, one should Fast the day of Wednesday, because no past community has been Punished except during the day of Wednesday in the middle of the month. Thus, it is recommended that one Fasts that day’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
there is fasting on Wednesday because for all nations upon which torment descended, it occurred on a Wednesday in the middle of the month. It is desirable to fast on that day.”
